output.brief: The rejects come from the combination of Arnholt resin and the degraded dryer D5 on Press 5. Neither factor alone causes them. Press 5 on Arnholt rejects about 10% on both shifts. Press 5 on Quillan rejects 0.9%. Press 7 rejects under 1% on either resin. Arnholt resin is wetter than Quillan when it reaches the dryer (0.27–0.33% against 0.11–0.14%). D5 cannot dry it below the 0.20% limit. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good dryer gave 0.8% rejects. The new operators are not the cause. They match experienced operators on each resin, and the shift gap only reflects that second shift runs Press 5 alone. Don't discipline them. Dropping Arnholt isn't needed either. This week, repair D5 (heater and desiccant) and verify its dew point is back to −40 °C. Restore the −40 alarm limit. Keep Arnholt off D5 until then, either on Press 7 or dried in a verified dryer. Check feed-throat moisture on every lot. One caveat: Arnholt was stored in the north annex and Quillan in the main warehouse, so storage may add to Arnholt's wetness. I'd test that before paying to move stock.
